name: Timeline: rail run
when: The voice says several dates in a row (2 to 6): the GTA games with their release years ("GTA III in 2001, Vice City in 2002 ... and in 2026, GTA VI: the first new GTA in 13 years"), or news dates without logos (Trailer 1, the two delays, Trailer 2, launch day). One rail; on each date the camera trucks along it to the next stop, the filled rail runs there, the game logo lands on the stop (or a node fills, for a date without a logo) and the date lands under it. The stop before keeps its logo or node and loses its text. On the last date the camera pulls back over the whole rail and the last stop lands bigger (hero). An optional gap label ("13 years") sits on the rail between two stops, on a segment twice as long.
anchor: at1 to at6: each step lands on the word that names it (the year, the event); the camera move, the rail fill, the logo and the date all start on that word and are still within 0.5 s. gap_at: the gap label lands on its words ("13 years"). The scene ends 0.23 s after `out`.
placement: Full screen on the video's ground: mount the clean ground (ground-B, or the darker ground-F or ground-G: one for the whole video) or ground-A (vice) under it with the same --start and the same length. Cut into it from the shot before and out of it to the next shot (the rail is its own shot). The whole scene counts as one graphic.

vars.theme: clean (on ground-B: white rail, nodes and text with a soft rose shadow) or vice (on ground-A: ink rail, nodes and text): the video's theme
vars.date1: step 1: the year or date the voice says, as it should read (2001, Dec 2023, 19 Nov 2026), at most 14 characters. Shown under its stop, 104 px (120 px on the hero stop). date2 to date6 the next steps; the steps stop at the first one with no date, label and logo (2 to 6 steps)
vars.label1: step 1: what happened, one to three words (Trailer 1, First delay, Launch), at most 22 characters; empty = none. Shown above its stop, 44 px. Use it for dates without logos; with a logo, leave it empty (the logo says it). label2 to label6 the next steps
vars.game1: step 1: the game, as logos.json names it (Grand Theft Auto III); it is the logo alt text. game2 to game6 the next steps
vars.logo1: step 1: its game logo file from assets/logos/ (gta_iii.png); empty = a date step (a node, no logo). A logo is never drawn or invented. build_video.mjs fills logo1 to logo6 (and their _cx) from game1 to game6 when assets/logos/ has that game. All steps should be the same kind: all logos (the series) or none (news dates)
vars.logo1_cx: step 1 logo: its visual centre in logo widths from its image centre (+ = right), from logos.json cx (GTA VI 0.091): the logo artwork centres on its stop and its date under it. logo2_cx to logo6_cx the same
vars.at1: seconds after the start: step 1 lands (the first word, 0.5 or later); at2 to at6 the next steps, each at least 0.6 s after the one before (the camera takes 0.5 s)
vars.gap: a gap label on the rail between two steps (13 years), at most 16 characters; empty = none. Its segment is drawn twice as long. It counts as a text: when it lands it takes the place of the older texts first, then of its own step label (the step date stays), so two texts at most are ever on screen
vars.gap_step: the gap sits just before this step (2 to 6); 0 = before the last step (between GTA V and GTA VI)
vars.gap_at: seconds after the start: the gap label lands (on "13 years"); 0 = with its step
vars.hero: true (default): the last step lands bigger (logo 1.6 times, date 120 px) and the camera pulls back over the whole rail, all logos in frame. false: the camera stays close and only trucks on
vars.out: seconds after the start: everything fades out together (the scene ends 0.23 s later); hold at least 1 s after the last step

source: new, built in the skills repo (lot 6, 17 Nov 2026); demo in algrow-gta-pipeline/lab/timeline/
